status.comment: schema and immutable receipt seam; package/publish integration and distribution evidence remain open

p.COMPONENT-RELEASE-FORMAT: A component release is a strict root object carrying descriptorSha256 and codkitComponentRelease:1, componentId, package/publish operation, immutable upstream revision and optional human label/resolution/provenance, patchset commit and config digest, declared type package/version/contract/manifest digest, discipline, generated commit/tree, artifact receipts, build recipe digest, selected licence-policy receipts, and distribution requirements/evidence. Unknown fields and unsupported versions refuse. SHA-256 receipt values and Git commit/tree object IDs are distinct types and algorithms; a Git object ID is never represented as a SHA-256 file digest.

p.COMPONENT-RELEASE-CANONICAL: Field order follows the single Zod schema. Artifacts and policies are sorted by identity; distribution lists are sorted by requirement using UTF-8 byte order. Duplicate identities, escaping artifact paths, empty distribution requirements and inconsistent completeness/missing lists refuse. descriptorSha256 hashes the canonical compact JSON of every root field except descriptorSha256 itself, including the format version. The stored descriptor is deterministic two-space UTF-8 JSON, LF-only, without BOM and with exactly one final LF. Readers validate the digest and exact canonical bytes; no migration or adapter execution is implied by reading a descriptor.

p.COMPONENT-RELEASE-IMMUTABLE: Receipts live at the contained patchset runtime path .codkit/releases/<descriptorSha256>.json. A writer validates data before I/O and publishes complete bytes only at an absent path through the existing atomic exclusive-link capability. Retrying identical bytes is idempotent; existing conflicting bytes, symlink parents/leaves and filename/body digest mismatch refuse without replacing the foreign file. This content digest establishes byte integrity, not origin authentication, legal compatibility, signing custody or authorization to deliver a release.

p.COMPONENT-RELEASE-ARTIFACTS: Artifact capture reads real selected outputs under a single physical root. Regular-file SHA-256 uses the existing contained descriptor proof and 64 KiB streaming buffer, with size/mtime/ctime stability checks. It returns absence for missing files, never an invented digest. Artifact paths and parents are contained; inode/mode/metadata checks refuse substitutions. Symlinks are represented by their exact UTF-8 link text bytes, never by following their target; a target escaping the physical root refuses.

p.COMPONENT-ARTIFACT-TREE: A directory digest is SHA-256 of compact UTF-8 JSON {codkitArtifactTree:1, entries:[...]}. Entries sort by UTF-8 path bytes; the root has path empty, and each entry names kind and permission mode masked by 07777. Empty directories are included. File/link entries additionally carry SHA-256 and payload byte count. Directory bytes is the sum of those payload counts, not a fictional archive size. This canonical tree stream is distinct from hashing a physical archive file; changing its rules requires coordinated descriptor/tree-format compatibility review.

p.COMPONENT-RELEASE-FACTS: Release fact capture proves configured upstream SHA/commit-date against actual Git objects and reads immutable generated commit/tree objects, effective canonical config, the explicitly supplied validated type declaration and a fresh validated installed supply-policy snapshot. Component identity defaults to the digest of sorted patchset history roots; shallow history requires an explicit component identifier. Recipe identity hashes JSON data without executing it. Missing organization policy, distribution notices or SBOM remain missing evidence, never invented approvals. Dirty package checkout and absent physical package artifacts remain explicit missing requirements alongside real Git object receipts.

p.COMPONENT-RELEASE-PACKAGE: The public package release operation verifies selected type/declaration identity before packaging, observes completed outputs before the existing unconditional scratch/overlay restoration, and publishes its descriptor only after restoration succeeds. It refuses a changed generated commit or patchset commit. Failed packaging/restore emits no successful descriptor. Artifact receipts are checked again after restoration; changed delivered bytes refuse instead of recording a stale pre-restoration digest. CLI package exposes the receipt path, digest, evidence status and missing requirements. --component-id supplies a stable explicit identity, including shallow repositories. The lower-level packaging worker remains available for established library callers and fixtures; release recording is a library capability rather than CLI-only logic.

p.COMPONENT-RELEASE-PUBLISH: The public publish receipt capability captures facts from the selected immutable patchset commit and the disposable checked checkout before delivery. The checked generated tip remains distinct from shaped/squashed/orphan delivered Git objects. Successful export/ref delivery records an immutable historical delivery receipt after the existing lease/tag transaction finishes and the disposable checkout is released; a failed gate or tag collision has no successful descriptor. Repeating an up-to-date immutable release is deterministic. Local receipt failure after delivery reports that delivery already succeeded and requests repair/retry; no cross-repository rollback or signing/legal approval is implied. Explicit type declarations come from a composition root or trusted registry, never patchset executable data.

p.COMPONENT-RELEASE-EVIDENCE: Completeness is relative to the explicit selected policy requirements and their actual evidence receipts. Emitters must obtain hashes from the objects and bytes they observed, name the licence-policy scope, retain unavailable evidence as missing and avoid inventing an external approval. The schema alone cannot attest how facts were obtained. Package/publish integration must bind the descriptor to the exact checked inputs and preserve package restore, publish leases, immutable tags and existing operation refusal behavior.

p.DECISION-COMPONENT-RECEIPT: Implement the source proposal's single-component release descriptor before a coordinator. Use a content-addressed immutable receipt rather than a mutable latest-release pointer: deterministic retries can compare exact bytes and conflicting data remains inspectable. Do not introduce signatures or organization commercial rulings without the corresponding external inputs. Revisit distribution requirements when P0.10 supplies trusted organization enforcement and real artifact evidence.
